title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

reports.title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

summary:
Rebecca Green agreed to let an AI scribe transcribe her first urologist appointment, but it invented a false claim that she micro-dosed psychedelic mushrooms. She discovered the error after kidney stone surgery in March, when a post-operative letter to her GP said mushroom use might explain earlier kidney bleeding. Ms Green, who was receiving workers' compensation, feared the false drug mention could hurt her case. After she complained, the urologist apologized, corrected the record, and said she would review how AI was used in her practice.

Australia's medical regulator says doctors must check all AI output, and the Royal Australian College of GPs estimates 40 percent of GPs regularly use AI scribes. A Digital Rights Watch report found other serious errors, such as recording the wrong breast in a cancer diagnosis. The Therapeutic Goods Administration is reviewing AI scribes and will release findings in coming weeks, with breaches to be acted upon. Patient advocates want approved tools tested, while Ms Green says she would only consent again with a doctor she already knows.
